question: The Prüm Convention allows the automated exchange of police data (DNA profiles, fingerprints, vehicle license plates) between EU Member States for the purpose of law enforcement and counter‑terrorism. Discussions are now taking place at EU level to expand aspects of the Prüm model to include non-EU countries, such as by introducing a legal framework entitled ‘Prüm International’ or similar agreements. 1.

Which non-EU countries does the Commission currently consider to be, in principle, suited to participating in ‘Prüm International’ or a comparable automated data exchange with EU Member States, when account is taken of their institutions, legal framework and level of data protection, and which non-EU countries have already expressed interest in taking part in the scheme?
What workshops or conferences has the Commission already held on this subject, and which non-EU countries, Schengen countries and EU agencies (such as Europol and euLISA) have taken part?
Is the Commission designing the ‘Prüm International’ framework on a ‘one size fits all’ basis, or are there plans for a legal framework tailored to each non-EU country?
answer: EN on behalf of the European Commission (3.7.2026) The Commission is assessing the possibility for a ‘Prüm international’ initiative. At this stage, the consultation and assessment phase for this new initiative are on-going. In that context, data protection standards, legal conditions and technical factors are being taken into account.

On 5 March 2026, the Commission services organised a technical workshop with Member States, the EU Agency for the Operational Management of Large-Scale IT Systems (eu-LISA) and the EU Agency for Law Enforcement Cooperation (Europol).

Schengen Associated countries joined for the final point included in the agenda of the workshop, during which the agencies presented their views and provided initial feedback on the ongoing reflections concerning the initiative. A public consultation has been launched on 12 June 2026 on the Commission’s website Have your say.
